more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
The US listing covers nutrient use under 21 CFR 184.1697; it does not establish a colour-additive listing (checked in 2026).
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Riboflavin-5'-phosphate sodium is a phosphate derivative of vitamin B2. It provides yellow colour under the EU E101(ii) specification. FDA also lists it as a nutrient ingredient, which is a different permitted function from colouring. The specified material is supplied as yellow powder or crystalline material.
more_info.origin: Made by chemically phosphorylating riboflavin. The sodium salt is supplied in a hydrated form; the FDA provision lists several phosphorylation reagents.
more_info.daily_intake: No ADI specified, as a group expressed as riboflavin (JECFA, 2021). This replaced the earlier 0–0.5 mg/kg body weight group ADI. EFSA did not allocate an ADI in 2013 because of incomplete long-term data.
more_info.side_effects:
At authorised food-use levels, EFSA found no safety concern in 2013.
For high combined intakes, evidence was insufficient to assess adverse effects.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
